story: On a sunny Monday morning at 10:17, Gary, Donna, and Rosa all set out for Magnolia Loop, each with a determined or hopeful stride. Hal stays home instead, settling into his porch chair to keep a watchful eye on the street. The town hums along under the 74-degree October sky as the neighbors converge on the Loop.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (hal porch chair): Sit on the porch and keep watch over the Loop
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: I've already dry-fit the wiring, soldered the connections, and sorted the toolbox. Everything in the garage is as ready as it can be without mounting anything, and L-01 says I can't put exterior mods on the cart until Architectural Review signs off. I filed the application back at tick 156 and checked the board at tick 206, but there was nothing new then. The Halloween parade is Saturday, so time matters. Rather than fiddle with the same wiring again, the useful move is to head out to Magnolia Loop, check the board for the board's decision, and see if Donna, Rosa, or Hal are around to talk parade details.

parameters.content: Heading out to check the bulletin board for the Architectural Review decision and see who's around about the parade.

donna.thought_process: I already penciled in practice on the calendar, packed the spare paddle, and texted Gary a practice time at ticks 207-209. He hasn't answered yet and nobody's nearby, so texting again would just be nagging. Better to do something productive toward the goal and the parade. Gary has never played, so I should head to the pickleball courts to scout open slots (keeping within the 2-hour reservation limit) and be ready when he replies. I'll also be near the Loop where Halloween cart planning can happen, all through Architectural Review properly.

parameters.content: Heading out to the Loop to scout where Gary and I can get court time and to catch him in person about practice and Halloween cart plans, since I've already texted him.

hal.thought_process: I've already scanned the Loop twice and logged the baseline: flamingos at three, no cart mods. Halloween decorations haven't gone up yet, so there's nothing new to report. Sitting here re-scanning an empty street accomplishes nothing. The parade is Saturday and decorations go up all week, so the sensible move is to settle in on the porch chair, keep an eye out, and be ready to document any ornament count over three or cart modifications as they appear. Order and respect, one hour at a time.

parameters.content: Sit on the porch and keep watch over the Loop

rosa.thought_process: Dinner went well last night, and Donna and Gary are on board for the Halloween parade. I've already pencilled in Tuesday and Thursday evenings three ticks running, so I shouldn't keep fiddling with the schedule. Nobody's around and it's a sunny Monday morning. The parade flyer says decorated carts are welcome all week, and I want our carts to stay within the rules (L-01 requires Architectural Review for exterior mods), so the useful next step is to get over to Magnolia Loop, see where neighbors are, and start the cart-decorating conversation with the whole Loop.

parameters.content: Heading out to the Loop to catch the neighbors and talk through decorating carts for the Halloween parade, keeping everything within the rules.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
